tests.notes: ~ on an unsigned integer flips only the bits within the type's width: ~uint8(0) == 255, ~uint256(0) == type(uint256).max
bitwise operators act on the two's complement bit pattern including the sign bit; andS(-2, 3) == 2
x ^ x == 0 and (x ^ k) ^ k == x
bitwise operators on different-width integers of the same signedness widen the narrower operand; result has the wider type
AND with a mask extracts bits; AND with the inverted typed mask (~uint256(0xFF)) clears them
set via OR, clear via AND-NOT, toggle via XOR with a constant mask
no implicit common type between signed and unsigned integers for bitwise operators, even at the same width
bool is not an integer type; &, | and ^ do not apply, use &&, || and !
unary ~ does not apply to bool; logical negation is !
address is not an integer type; bitwise operators need an explicit conversion to uint160 first
no implicit conversion between integers and bytesN, so there is no common type for a bitwise operation
~0 is the literal -1, which cannot be implicitly converted to an unsigned type; use ~uint256(0) or type(uint256).max
